newsitem.title: JAPAN: Weak yen has no major impact on Japan economy--EPA.
newsitem.headline: Weak yen has no major impact on Japan economy--EPA.

text.p: The yen's recent weakening is not having any major negative impact on Japan's economy or overall domestic prices, Economic Planning Agency (EPA) Vice Minister Shimpei Nukaya told a news conference on Friday.
He also said that an excessive fall or rise in the yen's value was not favourable for the economy, and currency stability was desirable.
"The yen's recent weakness is having no major demerit on the economy and overall prices," Nukaya said.
"Either an excessive fall or rise in the yen's exchange rate is not favourable (for the economy). Stability is the best thing," he added.

Commenting on Japan's diffusion index of leading economic indicators for November, released earlier on Friday, which showed a figure of 77.8 on a scale of 100, he said Japan's economy was showing that it was in a continuing recovery and there were no signs of any imminent setbacks to halt that.

He said financial markets had a sense of uncertainty about the direction of Japan's economy, and the government needed to quickly implement a supplementary budget for the current fiscal year ending on March 31 and the full state budget for 1997/98 in order to restore the markets' confidence in the government.
